subject: rent comps and how to read them
preheader: median is a lie. here's what to actually look at.
headline: Rent comps are the single biggest source of bad underwriting.
body: Rentometer, Zillow Rent Zestimate, RentCast, Apartments.com — every source gives a slightly different number, and the spread can be huge. I've seen a single property where the four major sources ranged from $1,750 to $2,400. That's 37%.

Median can lie. If a Rentometer report shows median rent of $2,000 with a range of $1,400-$2,800, the variance is doing you no favors. You need to understand WHY the range is that wide. Different neighborhood blocks? Different bedroom counts in the sample? Newer vs older stock?

What I do: pull two automated sources, then check actual active listings within a half-mile for the same beds/baths/size. The active listings are the real signal. Sold rentals (if you can find them through an agent friend) are even better. Zestimate alone is a starting point, never the answer.

Underwrite conservative. If the range is $1,700-$2,100 with median $1,900, model $1,750 unless you have specific reason to go higher. The downside of being conservative is mild — you miss a deal. The downside of being optimistic is a property that doesn't cover its mortgage.
TrueCap pulls multiple comp sources and shows the spread so you can see the disagreement before you trust any single number.
